import { Backpack, Blocks, CheckCircle2, FlaskConical, ReceiptText, Search, ShieldCheck, Terminal, TriangleAlert } from 'lucide-react';

Deploy an SVM program with the Solana CLI, inspect the deployed program account, estimate deployment funding, and manage upgrade authority.

## Command reference

Use these commands for the common deployment lifecycle.

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Build program | `cargo build-sbf` |
| Deploy new program | `solana program deploy <path_to_program.so>` |
| Update existing program | `solana program deploy <path_to_program.so>` |
| Show program metadata | `solana program show <PROGRAM_ID>` |
| List programs you control | `solana program show --programs` |
| Transfer upgrade authority | `solana program set-upgrade-authority <PROGRAM_ID> --new-upgrade-authority <path_to_keypair>` |
| Make immutable | `solana program set-upgrade-authority <PROGRAM_ID> --final` |
| Close program | `solana program close <PROGRAM_ID> --bypass-warning` |

## What you need

Prepare these before you build or deploy.

| Item | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Solana CLI | Builds, deploys, and manages programs |
| Rust toolchain | Builds native Rust programs |
| Program binary | The compiled `.so` artifact in `target/deploy` |
| Funded keypair | Pays deployment, account allocation, and transaction fees |
| Gorbagana RPC | Points the deploy command at Gorbagana |
| Explorer | Verifies the signature and program account |

<Callout type="info" title="Anchor projects">
  If this is an Anchor workspace, you can use the Anchor flow instead. Anchor wraps the same program deployment model with workspace config, IDLs, and generated clients.
</Callout>

## Program deployment model

Solana-compatible programs use the upgradeable loader model. These names appear in CLI output and explorer views.

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Program ID | The on-chain address clients use when they call your program |
| Program account | The executable account at the Program ID; it stores program metadata and points to ProgramData |
| ProgramData account | The account that stores deployed executable bytes and upgrade authority metadata |
| Upgrade authority | The keypair that can update, transfer authority, make immutable, or close the program |
| Buffer account | A temporary account the loader uses while uploading new program bytes |

Keep the upgrade authority keypair secure. If you lose it, you cannot update or close the program. If you remove it with `--final`, the program becomes immutable.

## Lifecycle overview

Most programs move through the same lifecycle.

| Stage | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Build | `cargo build-sbf` creates the compiled `.so` file and usually a program keypair in `target/deploy` |
| Deploy | `solana program deploy` uploads the executable bytes and creates the program account |
| Inspect | `solana program show` and the explorer confirm ProgramData, authority, size, balance, and slot |
| Update | Rebuild and run `solana program deploy` again while the upgrade authority still controls the program |
| Govern | Transfer upgrade authority, keep it secure, or remove it when the program should become immutable |
| Retire | Close the program only when it is no longer needed and still has an upgrade authority |

## Configure the CLI

Set Gorbagana as the active RPC endpoint and confirm the keypair that will pay for deployment.

```bash
solana config set --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
solana config get
solana address
solana balance
```

The wallet must hold native GOR. If it does not, bridge or send GOR to the address shown by `solana address`.

## Build the program

Build your native Rust program with the Solana SBF toolchain.

```bash
cargo build-sbf
```

The build writes deployable artifacts under `target/deploy`.

```txt
target/
  deploy/
    hello_gorbagana.so
    hello_gorbagana-keypair.json
```

The `.so` file is the compiled program. The `*-keypair.json` file controls the Program ID when your project generated one.

Print the Program ID before deployment:

```bash
solana address -k ./target/deploy/hello_gorbagana-keypair.json
```

If the keypair file is missing, rebuild the program or generate a new keypair for the program ID.

## Check program size and cost

Program deployments allocate storage for executable bytes. Larger programs need more native GOR than simple transfers.

Check the compiled program size.

<Tabs items={["macOS/Linux", "Windows PowerShell"]}>
<Tab>

```bash
wc -c < ./target/deploy/hello_gorbagana.so
```

</Tab>
<Tab>

```powershell
(Get-Item .\target\deploy\hello_gorbagana.so).Length
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

Use the byte count to estimate rent exemption:

```bash
solana rent PROGRAM_SIZE_BYTES
```

Keep more native GOR than the rent estimate because deployment also pays transaction fees and may need extra allocation if you later deploy a larger binary.

<Callout type="info" title="Solana CLI labels">
  Some Solana CLI output keeps Solana naming. When the CLI points to Gorbagana RPC, deployment fees and balances use native GOR.
</Callout>

## Deploy with the Solana CLI

From the program repository, deploy the compiled `.so` file to Gorbagana.

```bash
solana program deploy ./target/deploy/hello_gorbagana.so \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

Replace `hello_gorbagana.so` with the compiled artifact from your project.

Expected output includes a program ID and a transaction signature.

```txt
Program Id: PROGRAM_ID
Signature: TRANSACTION_SIGNATURE
```

Save both values. The program ID is the on-chain address your clients will call. The signature is the deployment transaction you can inspect.

To deploy with a specific Program ID, pass the program keypair explicitly:

```bash
solana program deploy ./target/deploy/hello_gorbagana.so \
  --program-id ./target/deploy/hello_gorbagana-keypair.json \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

## Inspect the program

After deployment, open the [Explorer](/network/explorer). Search for the program ID to confirm that the program account exists. Search for the transaction signature to review logs and fees.

You can also confirm the deployment transaction from the CLI:

```bash
solana confirm TRANSACTION_SIGNATURE -v \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

Show program metadata from the CLI:

```bash
solana program show PROGRAM_ID \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

Expected output includes the Program ID, owner, ProgramData address, upgrade authority, last deployed slot, data length, and balance.

```txt
Program Id: PROGRAM_ID
Owner: BPFLoaderUpgradeab1e11111111111111111111111
ProgramData Address: PROGRAMDATA_ADDRESS
Authority: UPGRADE_AUTHORITY
Last Deployed In Slot: SLOT
Data Length: PROGRAM_SIZE_BYTES
Balance: BALANCE
```

## Update a program

Update a program when the current upgrade authority still controls it.

1. Change the program source.
2. Rebuild the program:

   ```bash
   cargo build-sbf
   ```

3. Deploy the new binary:

   ```bash
   solana program deploy ./target/deploy/hello_gorbagana.so \
     --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
   ```

If the new binary is larger than the currently allocated program data account, the CLI can extend the program account during deployment and charge the fee payer for the extra allocation.

To extend space manually, use:

```bash
solana program extend PROGRAM_ID ADDITIONAL_BYTES \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

Use manual extension when you want to allocate space before a planned larger update. `ADDITIONAL_BYTES` is the extra space to add, not the final program size.

## Manage upgrade authority

Transfer upgrade authority when another keypair should control future updates.

```bash
solana program set-upgrade-authority PROGRAM_ID \
  --new-upgrade-authority ./new-authority-keypair.json \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

After the transfer, the old authority cannot update or close the program unless it has access to the new authority keypair.

Make a program immutable only when you are sure it should never change again.

```bash
solana program set-upgrade-authority PROGRAM_ID \
  --final \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

<Callout type="warn" title="Immutable means permanent">
  After you remove upgrade authority, the program cannot be updated or closed.
</Callout>

## Close a program

Close a program only when you no longer need it. Closing withdraws the account balance to the authority, but the Program ID cannot be reused.

```bash
solana program close PROGRAM_ID \
  --bypass-warning \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

If you later redeploy the same source, generate a new program keypair and use the new Program ID.

## Utility commands

Use these commands to audit programs controlled by your current CLI wallet or inspect deployed bytes.

List programs where the current wallet is the authority:

```bash
solana program show --programs \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

Download the deployed program bytes:

```bash
solana program dump PROGRAM_ID ./downloaded_program.so \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

Compare the downloaded file with your local build when you need to verify what is live.

## Deployment flags

Use these flags when uploads expire, the network is busy, or your deployment needs a specific fee strategy.

```bash
solana program deploy ./target/deploy/hello_gorbagana.so \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf \
  --max-sign-attempts 10 \
  --with-compute-unit-price 10000
```

| Flag | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `--max-sign-attempts` | Retries signing with a fresh blockhash when deployment transactions expire |
| `--with-compute-unit-price` | Adds a priority fee per compute unit |
| `--use-rpc` | Sends through the configured RPC path; use only if your RPC setup supports it |

## Common issues

<Accordions type="single">
<Accordion title="The deploy wallet has no native GOR">

Run:

```bash
solana address
solana balance
```

Fund that exact address with native GOR before deploying. Program deployments cost more than simple transfers because they write program data accounts.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="The CLI is pointed at the wrong network">

Run:

```bash
solana config get
```

The `RPC URL` value should match the Gorbagana endpoint in [Addresses](/reference/addresses).

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="The compiled file path is wrong">

Check that the `.so` file exists before deploying:

```bash
ls target/deploy
```

Use the exact file path in `solana program deploy`.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="The Program ID changed unexpectedly">

Check which keypair controls the Program ID:

```bash
solana address -k ./target/deploy/hello_gorbagana-keypair.json
```

Use `--program-id ./target/deploy/hello_gorbagana-keypair.json` when you need the deployment to use that exact Program ID.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="The upgrade authority is wrong">

Show the program metadata:

```bash
solana program show PROGRAM_ID \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

Check the `Authority` field. Future updates must be signed by that authority.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Deployment fails after submission">

Search the transaction signature in the explorer. Review the status, logs, account changes, and fee payer balance.

If the transaction never appears, rebuild and redeploy with a fresh blockhash instead of reusing an old serialized transaction.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="The update is larger than the deployed program">

Check the current data length:

```bash
solana program show PROGRAM_ID \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

Then compare it with the new local binary size:

```bash
wc -c < ./target/deploy/hello_gorbagana.so
```

If you want to allocate space before deploying, extend the program by the extra bytes you need.

```bash
solana program extend PROGRAM_ID ADDITIONAL_BYTES \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="The program cannot be updated">

Show the program metadata:

```bash
solana program show PROGRAM_ID \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

If `Authority` is missing, the program is immutable. It cannot be updated or closed. If `Authority` is present, sign the update with that authority.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="The deployment upload expires">

Increase signing attempts and retry with a fresh blockhash.

```bash
solana program deploy ./target/deploy/hello_gorbagana.so \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf \
  --max-sign-attempts 10
```

If uploads keep expiring, check RPC health and retry from a more stable network connection.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>
